title: A Multi-Labeled Dataset for Indonesian Discourse: Examining Toxicity, Polarization, and Demographics Information
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures how including annotator demographic information, specifically their religious identity, affects the performance of models in classifying toxic and polarizing Indonesian online discourse. It also examines the agreement gap on these classifications between different religious groups.
findings: Including annotator's religious identity, along with ethnicity and domicile, as a demographic feature significantly improves the performance of the IndoBERTweet model for both toxicity and polarization detection. The 'Best' performing setup for this model explicitly used religion. However, religion was not identified as one of the top three most polarizing identity markers among annotators, which were disability, residence in Jakarta, and Gen X age group.
